notes:
Qualification notes:
- Vertical: capital markets shop (quant + research) with strict data residency rules (US-only).
- Workloads: near-real-time chat for desks (p99 latency target 150ms internal), embeddings/reranking for search indexing (~100k reqs/day).
- Core ask: Private VPC deployment in customer AWS account (preferred us-east-1 + us-west-2 DR).
- Network topology preferences: private subnets for inference nodes, no public ENIs; NAT gateway for controlled outbound to S3 endpoints; prefer VPC endpoints (S3, KMS) and interface endpoints for control plane if possible.
- Inbound rules: only from customer app subnets through internal ALB -> target group; no direct internet inbound.
- Egress controls: strict egress filter, allow list for Redpanda/SQS endpoints; IDS/IPS in-line per SecOps.
- KMS: BYOK requested. Needs support for AWS KMS CMK import or custom HSM integration (key rotation policy + audit trail).
- Audit logging: push inference logs + auth events to Splunk; retention asked: 5 years for audit logs, 1 year for usage traces. Must redact prompt tokens per policy before long-term storage.
- Compliance: SOC2 required; ISO27001 referenced. CISO flagged data residency + immutable audit trail as hard requirements.
- Scale: initial pilot 2 GPU nodes (A100 equivalent), ramp to dedicated 8-16 GPUs for production. Autoscale but within reserved pools.
- Routing/fallback: want local model first, fallback to hosted Redwood snapshot if capacity constrained — confirm encryption of in-flight cache and KV.
- Integrations: SSO via SAML, SCIM provisioning, API gateway IP allowlist.
- Cost sensitivity: high at scale; Redwood Optimize recommendations + batching will be key discussion point.
- Quote: engineering team asked for architecture diagram + runbook (network, KMS setup, certs) to include in procurement package.
- Quote from CTO on call: "We cannot have prompt data leave our VPC unencrypted or be stored outside US without explicit approval."
- Stated blocker: procurement needs estimated TCO for private deployment vs dedicated reserved with egress patterns.
architecture_fit_summary: Customer prefers Private VPC in their AWS account in us-east-1 with DR in us-west-2. Target topology: private subnets across 3 AZs, NAT gateway for controlled egress, interface VPC endpoints for control plane, S3 VPC gateway endpoints for model artifacts. Option A: VPC peering + route table entries for Redwood control-plane endpoints; Option B: Transit Gateway for multi-account scale. KMS BYOK via imported CMKs; HSM option to be evaluated. Audit logs forwarded to Splunk via Kinesis Firehose. Expected constraints: no public load balancer exposure, egress allowlist, 5-year log retention, SOC2/ISO check required.
sales_play_notes: Use POC playbook: 1) deliver minimal VPC diagram + runbook, 2) small pilot (2 GPU nodes) in customer VPC, 3) validate KMS BYOK + audit log forwarding, 4) joint security review with CISO, then procurement cycle. Emphasize predictable unit economics (dedicated pool + optimize).
